description_en: After a woman's death her daughter or son advises the father to marry a neighbour, a teacher, etc., who usually herself talks the child into giving such advice. Having married the widower, the new wife begins to tyrannize her stepdaughter or stepson.

title_en: The heroine is turned into a dove
description_en: A woman turned into a dove through the intrigues of her rival tries to get in touch with her children or her husband.
A person thrown into the water is embodied in a flower (usually a lotus).
A youth obtains a girl who is inside a pomegranate.
A youth obtains a girl who is inside an orange or another citrus fruit.
A youth obtains a girl who is inside a gourd, an aubergine or a cucumber.
A youth obtains a girl who is inside an egg.

A youth receives several fruits (eggs, reeds). When he opens the first one, the girl who comes out of it disappears because what she needs (usually drinking water) has not been prepared or because the fruit was cut in the wrong way. Only the girl who comes out of the last fruit (egg, reed) remains. Cf. motif K33c7.

title_en: One fruit with a girl in it
description_en: A youth obtains a fruit out of which a girl comes (rare: two girls out of two fruits, both stay with the youth). There is no episode of losing the girls who were in other fruits. Cf. motif K33c6.
A youth obtains a girl who is inside a nut (a walnut or a hazelnut but not a coconut).
A youth obtains a girl who is inside an apple.

title_en: A spring of oil by vow
description_en: A person promises to make a spring from which a valuable product (most often oil) flows and honestly keeps the promise (rare: promises to give away a large amount of such a product).

title_en: To exchange an old ring for a new one
description_en: The hero's wife (mother, servant) does not know about the magic properties of an object kept in the house and exchanges it for something more attractive that in fact cannot compare with it in value.

title_en: A rival lures onto a swing
description_en: A rival puts a woman on a swing to get rid of her by throwing her into the water. The woman (almost) drowns or temporarily loses her human shape but manages to return to the world of people.
Person lights a room with a light-emitting object (usually a feather) that he has found.
Person finds a feather whose touch brings health and beauty.

title_en: The hero in the underwater kingdom
description_en: When a ship suddenly stops, the hero descends to the bottom of the sea, behaves correctly with its inhabitants and returns to the ship.
For a reason that is not clear at once a ship stops in the middle of the sea (rare: a horse stops in the middle of the road).

title_en: To identify a woman by her missing little finger
description_en: A man must identify his chosen one blindly. He does it by touch, knowing that one of her fingers is damaged or missing.
A clairvoyant cannot point out the one who gave away a secret because that one does it hiding among objects that are never found together in ordinary life.
A mighty bird helps a man because he fed its nestlings.
A mighty bird (rarely another creature) helps a man (rare: a woman) because he sheltered (warmed) its nestlings (young, children).

title_en: The hero shelters the sleepers from the sun
description_en: Seeing sleeping sorceresses or their children, the hero shelters them from the scorching rays of the sun. For this they do him good.

title_en: A serpent comes out of the water
description_en: The nest of a mighty bird is on a tree in the middle (at the edge) of a body of water out of which a serpent (monster) that threatens the nestlings comes.

title_en: A girl sacrificed to the dragon
description_en: For fear of a monster that lives in the water or to stop a flood or a drought, a girl is sacrificed or she herself willingly disappears into the waters.

In a series of three (more rarely two or four) places or objects associated with materials of high but different value, the highest value belongs to a precious stone (usually diamond; also glass, crystal).

title_en: A palace of gold and silver bricks

description_en: Person gets wild animals (of no less than two different species) that serve him like dogs.
A man sails away from a woman or a girl in a boat or on a raft. When she tries to grasp the edge of the boat (raft), he chops off her fingers. The fingers turn into aquatic animals.

title_en: A woman becomes an aquatic animal
description_en: A man and a woman of different generations (father and daughter, son and mother) come into conflict, as a result of which the woman turns into a sea mammal, the mistress of sea mammals or a frog.

title_en: A smile on the faces of the dead
description_en: The bodies of the killed are left in such a position that they seem to rejoice: to smile, laugh, dance.
A person is told to wash something black white or something white black (yarn, clothes, a board, etc.).
A stepmother sends her stepdaughter to a house in the forest and gives her ashes, sand, etc. instead of provisions. With the stepdaughter they turn into flour, groats, etc.
After meeting a supernatural person a kind person receives valuables, and a greedy one burns to death after coming back home.
After meeting a supernatural person the unkind girl becomes ugly.

title_en: The ugly one: growths on the face
description_en: After meeting a supernatural person growths (a tail, horns, warts, etc.) appear on the face (the back of the head) of the unkind girl.
A person gives a friendly answer to the question of persons who embody the weather of particular months of the year and is rewarded. Another scolds them and is punished.
A person gives a friendly answer to the question of a person who embodies cold, praises him and is rewarded. Another expresses displeasure and is punished.

title_en: The girl's hand in the cobra's hole
description_en: A well-behaved girl (usually a dog's daughter) wants to kill herself and puts her hand into a snake's hole. The snake does not bite her but gives her gifts.

title_en: The one who married a dog
description_en: A youth brings an animal home and it turns into a girl. Imitating him, another marries a dog (pig) but it remains an animal.

A girl agrees to become the wife of a serpent and he turns into a handsome man. Another girl (or her mother, father) herself brings a serpent home or offers a serpent to become his wife, but he does not turn into a man and kills her.

title_en: A row of gems and a row of logs
description_en: A girl finds herself in a forest hut and a bear comes there. He tells her to make him a bed of stones and logs.

title_en: The old man with golden coals
description_en: A poor man goes in search of fire. An old man by a campfire gives him coals. At home they turn into gold. An envious neighbour (brother) deliberately puts out the fire in his house and asks the old man for coals. His house burns down.

A supernatural being (object) gives riches to a modest man. A greedy one, trying to take more than is due, is seized and cannot free himself (for a long time). Usually the being clamps the outstretched hand.
A man's intestinal gases become fragrant. An envious person tries to achieve the same and the result is the opposite.

title_en: A song naming the days of the week
description_en: A man sees dwarfs (spirits, witches) making merry. The names of the days of the week are mentioned in their song. The man joins in naming the days whose names the dwarfs like. He is rewarded. (Usually another tries to get the same reward but names the wrong days of the week and is punished).

Five chickens (geese, etc.) must be divided among six eaters (other numbers are possible). The solution is to give one chicken to each pair of participants and to take two for oneself (two chickens and one man make three, two men and one chicken also make three).
To detain a beauty who runs away, a man in love with her smears the threshold (porch) with pitch or glue. Her slipper sticks; it is tried on all the girls and its owner is found.
A prince puts a ring on the finger of a beauty, not knowing that she is the very girl who works in his kitchen. The girl slips the ring into the prince's food and he recognizes it.

title_en: The tight slipper, the cut-off toes
description_en: A prince will marry the one whom the slipper fits. A girl cuts off her toes or her heel to get the slipper on.

title_en: The daughter is talked into killing her mother
description_en: Through her simple-mindedness or by accident a young girl causes her mother's death.
A dangerous person takes two people sleeping (hiding) in a sack or two people lying with their feet towards each other for one creature.

title_en: A man nurses a wounded eagle
description_en: A man rescues (spares) and nurses a wounded bird. Having regained its strength, the bird puts him on its back and carries him to a distant land or to the sky.

title_en: The Cyclops is blinded by a smith
description_en: The man who puts out or burns out the only (seeing) eye of the Cyclops is a smith.
A woman or a female animal gives birth to several sons, a man and a tiger among them.

title_en: Eve is ashamed of having many children
description_en: A woman (alone or with her husband) hides some of her children from God because she is ashamed of having produced so numerous offspring.
A woman acts as midwife (godmother) for a being that in the world of people has the guise of a toad or a frog.

A bear (lion) takes a woman to his place or a she-bear takes a man. Children of human or bear shape are born to them. More rarely the woman gives birth to a son in the den because she was pregnant when the bear abducted her.
A boy who grew up (was conceived) in a bear's den (lion's cave) becomes a strong hero.

Somebody promises to perform his duties until he hears a bird that calls at a certain moment of the time cycle (of the year or of the day). Another person imitates the bird. The first one detects the deception.

title_en: To slaughter the sheep that looks at you
description_en: A fool or a rogue is told to slaughter the sheep (cow, bull) that looks at him, i.e. no matter which. He slaughters all of them because all of them looked.
Pretending to carry out his master's order, a farmhand cuts off the animals' lips (so that they seem to smile).

title_en: A bear in the cattle shed
description_en: When a farmhand is sent to a place where a predator should tear him to pieces, he tames it and at home lets it into the cattle shed (stable). As a result the predator destroys the master's livestock.

A farmhand is ordered to go straight or to get over an obstacle without breaking it. He kills and cuts into pieces the animals entrusted to him and throws the pieces over the fence, or breaks the fence though there is a passage in it nearby.

title_en: The child is replaced with a broom
description_en: Women who wish a new mother ill replace her baby with a broom (tell its father that his wife gave birth to a broom).

title_en: The child is replaced with a log
description_en: Having hidden or thrown away a newborn baby, women who wish its mother ill replace it with a piece of wood and/or tell its father that his wife gave birth to a piece of wood.

title_en: The child is replaced with a doll
description_en: Women who wish a new mother ill replace her baby with a statue or a doll (tell its father that his wife gave birth to a doll).

title_en: The child is replaced with a puppy
description_en: Women who wish a new mother ill replace her baby with a puppy (tell its father that his wife gave birth to a puppy). See motifs K73, K73A.

title_en: The child is replaced with a kitten
description_en: Women who wish a new mother ill replace her baby with a kitten (tell its father that his wife gave birth to a kitten). See motifs K73, K73A.

title_en: The child is replaced with a monkey
description_en: Women who wish a new mother ill replace her baby with a monkey (tell its father that his wife gave birth to a monkey).

title_en: The child turns into a tree
description_en: Women who wish a woman ill kill (throw away) her wonderful children. Trees (flowers) grow from their remains and later turn into people again.

title_en: The wonderful children: a sister and two brothers
description_en: A woman gives birth to three (and not two or many) wonderful children, two boys and a girl. They grow up and triumph over their enemies.

title_en: The wonderful children: brother and sister
description_en: A woman gives birth to a wonderful boy and girl. They are replaced with animals or objects and thrown away, but they survive and triumph over their enemies.
Lying on the marital bed, the impostor who took the place of the true wife hears the talk of her rival or of the rival's children and in the morning orders the bed to be destroyed.

title_en: Mother and child in a barrel
description_en: A woman with her newborn son (pregnant with a boy) or a girl with a youth is put into a barrel (box; rare: a boat) and set adrift in the sea (river).

title_en: To make a cauldron boil with a story
description_en: A cauldron must be brought to the boil by telling a story that is incredible and yet true.

title_en: Throw a nut as a keepsake
description_en: A person who is asked to count the nuts in a barrel (to take the nuts out one by one) accompanies his actions with a story that exposes the truth.

title_en: To fill a sack with truth
description_en: A person is asked to fill a sack (cauldron) with truth (lies, tales). He fulfils the demand by telling a story that exposes the truth.

title_en: Just as a mother could not eat her child
description_en: A woman is accused of actions that by her very nature she could not have committed. To refute the accusation, an example of something equally absurd and impossible is given, or it is pointed out that the other party takes the impossible on trust but does not believe in the possible.

title_en: The hero flies to his mother's enemies to overhear them
description_en: The wife of a powerful person gives birth to wonderful children. Her envious sisters arrange it so that the husband orders to get rid of his wife (usually to shut her in a barrel together with her child and throw it into the water). The boy grows up at once and saves his mother and himself. He himself (in the guise of a bird, animal or insect, or flying on a magic object) or his puppy brother gets into his father's place and, overhearing a conversation, learns about the existence of wonderful objects. Having returned, he obtains them, or he possesses them from the start and shows them when he meets his father (the youth's brothers can also be among these objects).

title_en: The hero kills the magic wife's enemy
description_en: The hero saves his magic wife from her enemy at the time when both the future wife and the enemy have zoomorphic guise. Later the rescued one becomes a woman.

title_en: The youngest son-in-law's place is in the cattle shed
description_en: A ruler orders his youngest daughter (with the husband she has chosen) to live in conditions that do not befit her status. He does not know that her chosen one is not the miserable pauper he seems to be but a hero and a handsome man.
Having come incognito to a powerful person, the hero works for him as a gardener.
Having come incognito to a powerful person, the hero works for him as a groom.
Wishing to show that it is time for them to marry, daughters of different ages send their father fruits of different ripeness (bread baked to a different degree).
The devil promises a man riches if he does not wash (cut his hair, etc.) for a certain time; both keep their promises.

title_en: A woman gave birth to a gourd
description_en: A woman gives birth to a gourd inside which there is a human being (many people) or which turns into a human being.
The son or foster child of a couple is a hedgehog. He marries a princess and turns into a handsome man.
The son or foster child of a couple is a crayfish (crab). He marries a princess and turns into a handsome man.

A youth who temporarily has a strange or monstrous guise (a freak, an animal, etc.) asks for the hand of a princess but is refused. Then he causes natural disasters or creates personal troubles for the king, and the king has to give his daughter.
To the predator's questions the he-goat (she-goat, ram, etc.) answers to the effect that parts of his body are weapons and other objects meant to kill the asker, or the he-goat is really armed.
Goats meet a wolf. One has one belly (stomach), the second has two, the third has three, etc. The goat with the greatest number of bellies kills or frightens the wolf.
A demonic person swallows cripples and regurgitates them healthy and better-looking.

title_en: To the forest to pick berries
description_en: Members of one family (girls, young women or children) go to the forest to pick berries and kill (bewitch) the one of them whom they envy.
Brothers who are rivals as suitors or heirs must get a boar. The youngest succeeds. The elder ones kill him and appropriate the boar. The truth comes out.

title_en: A talking pipe made from a plant that grew
description_en: A musical instrument is made of a plant that grew at the place where a person was killed (fell, touched the ground). When it is played, words of a certain content are heard.

title_en: A name helps to solve the murder
description_en: Before his death a man asks his murderer to tell his pregnant wife to give the newborn a certain name. Having heard the unusual name of the child, a person in power begins to investigate the case and the murderer confesses his crime. (All texts with motifs K80c3 and K80c4 also contain the more general motif K80c).

In a deserted place one man kills another. After some time he is exposed thanks to facts and circumstances that do not seem important and do not tell about the crime directly (the last words of the victim; objects or living beings that were or appeared at the place of the murder). (All texts with motifs K80c3 and K80c4 also contain the more general motif K80c).

title_en: The handless girl in the prince's garden
description_en: A girl whose hands have been cut off comes to a fruit tree (garden bed) to find food. Having seen her there, a prince marries her.
To fulfil a task, a person's sons must ride to a place where he has never been (or where he once was).

title_en: To give to the first who asks
description_en: Dying, a father tells his son to give his sister (sisters) in marriage, setting no conditions, to the one (those) who comes for her.

title_en: The horse whose hide cannot be bitten through
description_en: Having told to cover him with hides (to smear him with pitch and sprinkle him with sand, etc.), the hero's horse becomes invulnerable to the bites of another horse.
Magic horses live in the water.

title_en: Marriage with an animal ends badly
description_en: A woman becomes the wife of an animal (rarely of another non-human being). The husband takes care of her, but the marriage ends in the killing of the husband, the woman, their offspring or the woman's relatives, in her own transformation into an animal, leads to enmity between people and animals, etc.
A demonic woman asks the mother of a baby to let her hold it or secretly takes the place of another person who was to take the child. Having got the baby, the demon carries it away to her place.

title_en: A dog's blood will cure the princess
description_en: Person learns that the blood (brain, etc.) of the dog that guards a neighbouring herd will cure the princess (prince). He applies this remedy and is rewarded.

title_en: An elk dies after swallowing a mouse
description_en: A small animal (little bird, mouse, porcupine, fox) or (rarely) a tiny man lets himself be swallowed by a big ungulate (elk, deer, bison, tapir) in order to rip its belly open (and eat it).

title_en: A bear dies after swallowing a mouse
description_en: A zoomorphic person no bigger than a fox lets himself be swallowed by a bear and kills it ripping it open from inside.

title_en: The wife weaves, the husband sells
description_en: A princess or a sorceress becomes the wife of a poor man. She weaves or embroiders a kerchief (or another object) and sends her husband to sell it. This is the beginning of their way to success.
Person gets into the camp of his adversaries having taken the guise of a kitten or a puppy. Usually one of the adversaries suspects deceit but the others believe that the nice animal is harmless.

title_en: The sword that grew in the garden
description_en: Sons are born from a fish eaten by a woman, and from what was buried in the garden come objects that are later connected with these youths. These are either weapons (swords, sabres, rapiers) or objects by whose appearance one can tell what is happening to the youths.
Lovers are buried in one grave or close to each other. Two plants reaching towards each other grow at this place, and between them a thorny bush that embodies the person who separated the lovers.

title_en: The lucky dream: sun, moon and stars
description_en: A man sees in a dream the sun, the moon and stars (all together or some of them). At the end of the narrative the meaning of the dream becomes clear: these are the people who love him or who worship him (often two wives and a child).
A gull abducts a girl or a woman but she manages to return to people.

title_en: A jet of dung in the pursuer's face
description_en: The hero or the heroine flees from a demon riding a domestic animal (often a young bull). When the demon comes near, the animal discharges a jet of dung or intestinal gases into his face and he gives up the chase.

title_en: The protective little dog and the ogress
description_en: A little dog, a cat or another animal tries to drive away a demon (usually an old ogress). The demon (or its victims, who do not understand the danger themselves) kills the animal, usually by chopping off (breaking) parts of its body one after another, after which the demon gains power over its victims.

A man takes an object that belongs to another and loses it; the owner demands the object back; the hero goes after it (to the other world), usually finds the lost object and brings it back. See motifs K56a3 and L105.

title_en: A smith makes the voice thin
description_en: To make his voice thin, a person turns to a smith.
To get a thin voice, a person lets ants bite his tongue.
A person who swallowed his prey alive falls asleep. When his belly is ripped open, those swallowed are taken out and stones are put in their place, he notices nothing.

title_en: Imitation: a knife across the throat
description_en: To get rid of a dangerous but stupid person, a man performs certain actions which the person imitates, not understanding that he thus harms himself.
A man deliberately performs certain actions before a monkey's eyes. The monkey imitates him and harms itself.

title_en: The fighting hero wakes his brothers
description_en: The hero fights a serpent and calls for help but is not heard. Then he flings a piece of his footwear or clothing, and his brothers, now awake, or his horse come running.
To confuse the pursuer, a person leaves tracks leading in all directions before running away.

A person pulls a sinew, the spinal cord or an intestine out of a demon's body, cuts off a strip of its skin or receives a belt as a present, but does not gird himself or another person with it and puts the belt around a tree. The belt cuts or burns the tree.
A belt (sinew, gut, strip of hide, etc.) cuts or burns whatever it is applied to (a tree or a human being).

title_en: The werewolf wife suffers from thirst
description_en: The woman with whom a man lives is a being of non-human nature. It becomes clear after at night, suffering from thirst and finding no water in the house, she takes her true shape, turning into a snake, separating her limbs from her body, etc.
Having followed his wife (her husband), the husband (wife) discovers that she or he goes to devour corpses.

title_en: Why such big teeth? (Little Red Riding Hood)
description_en: A person is asked why parts of his body, organs or tools are the way they are. He answers (or the asker himself gives explanations for him). Eventually one kills or maims the other.

title_en: The human asks, the wolf explains
description_en: A wolf or a demon is asked why parts of his body or organs are the way they are. He explains them one after another.
To get rid of a demonic creature or to make a bird or a ladybird fly away, they are told that the place where their home and/or children are is on fire.

title_en: Your children are burning: addressed to a demon
description_en: To get rid of a demonic person (usually a woman), he or she is told that the place where his or her home and/or children are is on fire.

title_en: Your children are burning: addressed to a bird or ladybird
description_en: To make a bird or a ladybird fly away, it is told that the place where its home and/or children are is on fire.

title_en: Theft of food: a family conflict
description_en: When a member of a small (family) group, left alone, secretly eats the food, it leads to a serious conflict, often to the killing of the culprit.
A person keeps his limbs separately and joins them to his body when necessary.
The hero's adversary (usually a demonic woman) is inside a sea wave (the third, the ninth) or embodies the wave.

A man leaves home and finds himself in unfamiliar places. His way is marked by encounters with various strange beings. Eventually he returns home or leaves the earth for another world. (With its abundance of episodes, the story rather often either breaks off or lacks the initial episodes that explain why the hero left home).
The vulnerable spot of a person is at the bottom of the leg (heel, toe, sole, ankle).
A person's body is tempered (in a furnace, etc.) to make it invulnerable but one spot remains unprotected.
A dangerous person naively tells what exactly he is afraid of or where his life is kept, and the hero takes advantage of it.

title_en: The false receptacle of the soul
description_en: When somebody tries to find out from a person where his soul (death, strength) is, he gives a wrong answer at first, and the asker usually begins to show signs of attention to the place or object named.

title_en: What happened when you threw the sword into the lake?
description_en: One person tells another to throw a certain object (usually a sword or a sabre) into the water. The messenger claims that he has done it but cannot say what happened as a result, so it becomes clear that he lied.

title_en: A family member kills another knowing his secret
description_en: A person knows the secret on which the life of his or her close relative (husband, son, wife) depends and after a quarrel performs an act that means little to an outside observer but leads to the immediate death of the other.

title_en: The person's soul is in an egg
description_en: The object that contains a person's life is enclosed in another, that one in a third (and so on). The last receptacle of the soul is an egg (to kill the person, the egg must be broken against his head).

title_en: The person's soul is in a little bird
description_en: The object that contains a person's life is enclosed in another, that one in a third (and so on). The last receptacle of the soul is a bird (a nestling, several birds or nestlings).

title_en: The person's soul is in an insect (worm)
description_en: The object in which a person's life is concentrated is enclosed in another, that one in a third (and so on). The last receptacle of the soul is an insect or a worm.

title_en: The person's soul is in a needle
description_en: The object in which a person's life is concentrated is enclosed in another, that one in a third (and so on). The last receptacle of the soul is a needle; the hero breaks it.
Persons with a different, successively increasing number of eyes stay to watch the hero or the heroine. He or she puts the eyes to sleep one after another but forgets the very last one.

title_en: The rival with an eye in her forehead
description_en: Instead of a beautiful woman a man takes a she-devil with an odd number of eyes.

title_en: A creature with an even number of heads
Being with an odd number of heads
description_en: Beings (any except bird-like ones) with more than ten heads or with an odd number of heads (more than one) are described or represented (when beings are listed in order of increasing number of heads, the series ends with an odd number).

A monster (usually a reptile) with seven heads is described or depicted (except for cases when serpents with an ever greater number of heads are described in succession and seven is not the greatest number).
A being with nine heads is mentioned, alone or as the last in a series of beings with a smaller number of heads.
A being with twelve heads is mentioned, alone or as the last in a series of beings with a smaller number of heads.
A young woman turns into a she-bear (in Asia: a tigress) and attacks her close relatives or her husband.

title_en: The demon woman and her brothers
description_en: A woman comes into conflict with her brothers and turns into a dangerous demon.
Those who flee from the monstrous she-bear rise to the sky and turn into stars.

title_en: To break an object in half
description_en: Trying to get free, a seized person changes shape again and again. The last transformation is a small wooden object (usually a spindle). When this object is broken in half, the person acquires human shape for ever.
A man seizes a woman he desires. Trying to get free, she turns into various substances, materials and animals, or (Urarina, Setebo) tells various dangerous animals to attack the man who seized her.
A person seizes a male person. Trying to get free, the latter turns into various substances or animals.
During the (first) initiation men kill supernatural persons (and since then reproduce their appearance and/or voices during rituals).

title_en: The overheard talk: a snake inside a person
description_en: From a talk of snakes or ravens a man learns the cause of another's illness: a snake has crawled inside him. The man drives the snake out and the sick one recovers.

title_en: A bird's body has a miraculous effect
description_en: From a talk of birds a man learns that their bodies or excretions have a miraculous effect.

title_en: A dog's flesh has a miraculous effect
description_en: From a talk of spirits or animals a man learns that the flesh (brain, blood) of a neighbouring shepherd's dog has a miraculous effect.
A man meets the embodiments of Good Fortune (and Bad Fortune), his own or somebody else's. He manages to influence their behaviour and change the course of things for the better (for himself).
The Luck (Misfortune, Need, etc.) of every person is a particular being with whom the person communicates.
A boy climbs a tree for fruits. A demonic person asks him to share them, not throwing the fruits on the ground but handing them over. The demon seizes the boy and carries him away.

title_en: The buyer of the bridle leads the camel away
description_en: Relying on the ambiguity of a statement, the one who bought a cheap object claims a much more valuable one.
When a demon tries to shake the meat out of the sack over a cauldron, stones fall from the sack into the cauldron and it cracks, or the boiling water that splashes out scalds the demon.

title_en: Those who slid down the hill
description_en: An ogre seizes children when they are sliding down a hill.

title_en: Frying pans put one on another
description_en: A person abducted by a demon advises him to put pots, frying pans and other kitchen utensils one on another and climb up them. The demon does so, falls and is smashed.
In the forest or in the sky a person sees a house that is entirely or partly made of edible materials.

title_en: The ogre belches out an axe
description_en: A demonic person belches out an axe (adze) to cut down a tree.
A man and a demonic person agree to compare their lice. When the man shows a turtle or a frog, the demon believes that the man is more terrible and stronger than he.

To test the loyalty of the heroine (hero), a demon demands that she eat food that people must not eat. Usually when the heroine says that the food has been eaten, the demon asks the food where it is and the food answers him.

title_en: The blood cannot be washed off
description_en: A person learns that the taboo to enter a certain room has been broken because the evidence of it remains on the body of the heroine (hero) or on an object in her (his) hands (often it is blood on a key or an apple).

title_en: The demon woman pursues her children
description_en: A woman who has become a monster pursues her own children.

A demonic person devours part after part of the horse on which the hero came, each time returning to the hero and then leaving to devour one more part. (Often the demon asks whether the hero came on a three-legged, two-legged, one-legged horse).
A man shoots off (injures) a finger of a demonic creature and then sees that his sister lying in the cradle has lost a finger.
A man exchanges sheep (goats) for dogs. The exchange looks unequal but the dogs help him to succeed.
The hero's dogs have names that tell of their strength and agility (Wind, Break-Iron, etc.).
A person who has climbed a tree manages to escape from a demon (usually the demon tries to fell the tree).
A person pulls out his own tooth to use it as a weapon or a tool (often an axe).

title_en: The hero's dogs at the princess's wedding
description_en: In spite of obstacles, the youth's dogs or other animals that serve him get to the princess at the moment when she is about to be married to an impostor.
To destroy the obstacles created by the hero, the pursuer uses tools. Before continuing the chase, he has to spend time carrying them home or hiding them, otherwise animals and birds will steal them.

Fleeing, a person throws behind him a tool for making fire (fire-steel, a match, tinder), which turns into an obstacle in the pursuer's way. (A thrown flint is counted if it is used for striking fire and is not counted if it is just a hard stone that turns into a mountain).
Fleeing, a person throws behind him a piece of soap, which turns into an obstacle for the pursuer (a slippery mountain, a river, etc.).

title_en: An awl (needle) turns into many awls (needles)
description_en: Fleeing, a person throws behind him an awl or a needle, which turns into a multitude of awls or needles.

Fleeing, a person throws behind him a small vessel of oil. The spilled oil turns into a lake or a river. (Only North American materials are taken into account. In the Old World the motif is rare and unsystematic. In North America it is most probably hair oil in all cases).
Throwing some object behind him, a fleeing person creates fog or darkness in the pursuer's way.
The fugitive draws a line on the ground (ice), as a result of which an obstacle appears in the pursuer's way.

title_en: A kerchief opens and closes the way
description_en: Waving a piece of cloth (towel, kerchief, garment) or throwing it, putting it on the water, etc., a person creates obstacles (in the pursuer's way) or a means to overcome them (a bridge, etc.).

title_en: The legless, the blind and the armless
description_en: A legless man lives together with a blind man and an armless man (or with one of the two). Cooperating, they are healed.

title_en: After a fight the cripples recovered
description_en: Two cripples with different bodily defects quarrel and fight, and as a result become whole and healthy.
A person temporarily splits vertically into two halves and then joins together again.
Parts of a person's body have the form of cutting or piercing tools.

title_en: Lips nailed to sky and earth

description_en: Human heads are stuck on stakes near the house of a dangerous person and one stake has no head (or a wall is built of heads and one is missing). It is implied that the head of the hero of the narrative is to be there.
A monkey, resorting to cunning, helps the hero or the heroine and saves them.
A hedgehog, resorting to cunning, helps the hero and saves him.

title_en: Give me what you do not know at home!
description_en: A man promises to give a supernatural person the one who comes out first to meet him (or what he has not yet seen in his own house, or what is behind the door, etc.). The man thinks that he will have to give something of no great value, but it turns out to be his own child.

title_en: The demon gathers the wealth back into the casket
description_en: A man receives as a gift a box (bag, horn, etc.) that he must open only at home. Driven by curiosity, he opens it on the way and everything that was to make him wealthy (houses, livestock, etc.) pours out of it. A demon appears and agrees to put everything back but sets a condition whose gravity the man usually does not understand at once.
A demonic person accuses a man of having stepped on the tail (torn off the tail) of a tale. Cf. motif K100E, "Aggressive stories".
The supernatural person who helps the hero or the heroine on certain conditions is a white wolf.

title_en: Together with the demon against the child
description_en: Having promised to give their child to a demon, the mother or the father does not try to save it but arranges it so that the child falls into the demon's hands. In spite of everything, the son or the daughter escapes.
A youth learns magic. To make the sorcerer let him go, he must pretend to be incapable of learning.
A person has a nose or teeth of gold or silver, which is a sign of his demonic nature.
A man's hair or beard is of an unusual colour, which is a sign of his demonic nature.

title_en: Fire at the edge of a cliff
description_en: One person brings another to a precipice in order to make a fire, or makes a fire at the edge of a precipice. As a result the other falls and is smashed.
One person talks another into jumping from a high cliff or a tree because the other's ancestor allegedly did so. The other jumps and is smashed or falls into the clutches of the first.
A person hides his children but tells another that he has killed them. The other believes him and kills his own children. See motif M104.

title_en: The allegedly killed children: two birds
description_en: One of two birds, both of which (rare: only one) are flightless, suggests that the other break its eggs. The other agrees and then sees that the first one has kept its own.
A man puts his hat on the ground and pretends that there is something valuable under it. In fact there is dung there. The one who believes the deceiver loses his property.
A deceiver takes away in a boat or carries off other people's property. A little bird (usually a woodpecker) deceives him in turn and returns the property to its owners.

title_en: How many steps has your horse made?
description_en: A man (a powerful person) asks a girl (a subordinate) about the number of routine actions she has performed (or of small objects at hand) which obviously nobody counts. She asks a counter-question about the number of actions of the same kind performed by the asker.

title_en: Clothes from a bunch of flax and a loom from three sticks
description_en: When a girl is told to weave clothes from a negligible amount of yarn, she asks in return to make her weaving tools of little sticks, chips, a straw, etc.

title_en: Throws away the killed, brings the unkilled
description_en: A person answers that his father (brother, etc.) is hunting: those he notices he kills (throws away), and those he does not notice (does not kill) he leaves (brings with him). Lice or fleas are meant.

A man drags his father intending to leave him to die in a deserted place, to give him to an almshouse, to throw him into an abyss, etc. On the way he stops. The father says that he also stopped at this place when he dragged his own father. Or a boy asks to keep the sledge, hide, etc. on which his father drags the grandfather (or takes away half of the cloak with which his father covered the old man): it will be needed when he himself drags his father. Or the old man is given a wooden (broken, etc.) plate to eat from, and the boy says that he will give the same to his father when he grows old. The man brings his father back home (begins to take care of him).
A person makes food tasty by salting it. Another finds out that the cook extracts this salt from his own body (it is contained in his bodily excretions).
Animals, demons or people stand on one another to reach something. The lowermost one jumps aside (bends down, jerks), and all fall down after him.

The wolf (more rarely another predator) approaches various (more than one species) domestic animals (animals and people) to eat them but, agreeing to fulfil their request, remains hungry and usually beaten.

title_en: The wolf regrets his own stupidity
description_en: The wolf (rarely the bear, jackal, fox) approaches various domestic animals to eat them but, agreeing to fulfil their request, remains hungry and usually beaten, and in the end blames himself ("Am I a mullah to read?", etc.). In the Persian version the fox tells him this.

title_en: A hundred and twenty years of life

description_en: The stripes on the tiger's skin appeared after it was singed.

To get rid of fleas, the fox (jackal) takes a bunch of moss (hay, grass) in its mouth and sinks into the water. To avoid drowning, the fleas move closer and closer to its head and then get onto the moss or hay. The fox leaves the bunch in the water and comes out onto the bank.
A person pretends to be holding up a rock, a tree, etc. that is allegedly about to fall. See Dixon 1916: 189. (It is possible that in America the motif is of late African origin).
The tiger (lion) and another animal compete to see whose roar is louder. The tiger roars louder but loses in the end.

title_en: We will eat the one whose voice is quieter
description_en: Animals agree to eat the one of them whose voice is the quietest.

title_en: The pregnant wife on a mare in foal
description_en: A man who understands the language of animals hears a mare say that she is carrying four (three): she has a foal in her belly and the woman in the saddle is pregnant too.

A dangerous animal is going to kill a man or another animal that helped it. The predator and the victim agree to ask those they meet (who walk or float past) which of them is right. There are inanimate objects (most often a tree) among those who answer.

title_en: You think you see the abbot
description_en: To help a man answer a ruler's questions, his servant or friend takes his place and gives witty answers. Most often the ruler also asks what he is thinking now. The answer: you think that one man is before you, but in fact it is another.

Animals (mostly domestic) and/or people join their efforts one after another to reach a goal (usually to pull a root vegetable out of the ground). They succeed after the last participant (usually the weakest) joins in.
Two animal persons till a plot together. During the field work one idles (imposes his sham services on the other) and then claims (the greater) part of the harvest.
A man sells a cat (cock) to people who do not know about cats (or chickens). Having got the cat or the cock, the people do not know what to feed it with and fear that it eats people.

A father leaves his son (each of his sons) something of no particular value as inheritance. The son comes to a country where such objects or animals are unknown and sells what he received for a lot of money.

title_en: The rim of a vessel on the neck
description_en: A zoomorphic person puts his head into a vessel; it breaks and its rim remains on his neck. The person uses it as a proof of his high position.

title_en: In exchange for a bast shoe
description_en: A person has only a bast shoe with him (or later pretends that he had one). He asks for a night's lodging and in the morning claims that he had something more valuable with him. At every new lodging he goes on exchanging the less valuable for the more valuable.

title_en: The one who looks away ate it
description_en: One zoomorphic person teaches another to keep silent, to look at him or aside when a third one starts inquiring who ate the best piece. It is a trap: the third decides that the second is guilty.

title_en: Mother or grandmother deceive the blind man
description_en: The mother or grandmother of a blind man or boy eats in secret from him the meat or fish (that he obtained), pretending that there is no food in the house.

title_en: The wife deceives the blind man
description_en: A wife aims a blind man's arrow at the game, lies that he missed and eats the meat herself.

title_en: Who eats more: one against many
description_en: Two argue which of them can eat or drink more. One of them is constantly replaced by his relatives; the adversary does not notice the substitution and loses.
Two fishes (a fish and a whale or dolphin, a squid and a dolphin, etc.) agree to swim a race.

title_en: The harvest goes to the fastest runner
description_en: Two animal persons agree to give the harvest of the field they tilled together to the one who runs faster.

title_en: The race: crayfish or crab takes part
description_en: Taking part in a race, the crayfish (crab) defeats a faster rival.

title_en: The snake will not forget its cut-off tail
description_en: A man does good (does no harm) to a snake (fish, lion) and profits from it. His son (more rarely somebody else or he himself) wounds the snake (usually cuts off its tail) and, if it is the son, dies of its bite. The snake refuses to continue relations with the man: neither of them will forget their loss.
By singing (threats, compliments) the wolf (more rarely the bear) forces an old man to give him his domestic animals (and family members) one after another.

A woman baked a flat cake (pancake, pie, dough man). It rolled (ran) away. On its way it meets various people and/or animals who want to eat it. It rolls on from each of them, but the fox (rarely another animal) eats it.

title_en: Which end of the stick is the upper one?
description_en: A person sends a long object that either looks the same at both ends or is inside a small object and demands to tell which end of it is the upper and which the lower one. The solver gives the correct answer.

title_en: The clever or the lucky one solves riddles
description_en: People of high status cannot determine the hidden difference between two or several outwardly similar objects or beings, or between two sides of one object or being. A man of low status does it thanks to his own wit or to chance.

A demon claims that the harvest in a man's field belongs to him. But if the man brings an animal unknown to the demon, he will give up his claims. The man brings his wife smeared with something sticky and rolled in feathers, on all fours, with her hair let down, etc. The demon admits his defeat.
A man who cannot find lost things or expose thieves does it successfully thanks to a lucky coincidence.

title_en: The sham soothsayer: the thieves' names
description_en: Expecting to be exposed, a sham soothsayer utters words that reflect his state of mind. The thieves who are nearby take some of the words for their own names, think that the soothsayer has found out about them and ask him not to give them away.

title_en: The sham soothsayer: the overheard talk
description_en: A sham soothsayer accidentally overhears somebody's talk; otherwise he would not have been able to give the right answer.

A powerful person tells a man to guess what is in his casket. The man says that now he, So-and-so, is caught, or utters an exclamation. This exclamation or name sounds like "toad" or "frog", and the person believes that the man has a special gift.

A giant sends a man for water giving him a huge waterskin. The man cannot lift so much water but gets out of the difficulty by cunning (pretends that he wants to bring the whole well at once; that he has already brought the water and drunk it all himself; etc.).

title_en: Persuades the adversary that he can fly
description_en: When a giant blew, sneezed, etc. or let go of a bent tree on which a man was sitting, the man was thrown far away. The man says that he did it of his own will (to show how he can fly, to mend the roof, etc.).
A man explains to a demon that heavy objects lying by the road, such as a harrow or a millstone, are just small things used by his grandmother or mother, such as a spindle whorl or a comb.

title_en: To fill a hat with a hole with gold
description_en: A man suggests that a demon fill a hat, a sack, etc. with money. The demon does not notice that there is a hole in the hat and gives the man much more than he intended.
A man and his adversary agree to make a hole in a tree trunk (stump) with the head (finger, penis) or to fell a tree with a blow of the head. The man made the hole (sawed into the tree) in advance.

title_en: The old donkey carries the young one
description_en: An old man and a boy set off taking a donkey with them. They try all the options: only the old man rides the donkey, only the boy, both together, both walk beside the donkey, they carry the donkey themselves. Each time people make unflattering comments.
A mushroom (melon) that grew fast believes that it will soon outgrow the oak. The mushroom (gourd vine) soon rots and the oak stands as it stood.

title_en: To pull a splinter from the lion's paw
description_en: A man pulls a splinter out of the paw (a bone out of the throat) of a strong and dangerous animal or demon, who is grateful.

A supernatural being sends a certain message to an unknown addressee through a man it meets. Having fulfilled the request, the man provokes a reaction, unexpected for him, of another supernatural being (usually one living in his house). Most of the material was collected by K. Yu. Rakhno.

title_en: Pass on that I have died
description_en: A supernatural being sends a message to an unknown addressee through a man it meets; having delivered it, the man perishes or suffers damage.

title_en: The cat is connected with spirits
description_en: A man learns that a cat he knows, which lives in the human world, belongs at the same time to the world of spirits.

title_en: The money goes to the one destined for it
description_en: When a deity (a powerful person) tries to pass valuables to a man, he gets them or does not get them in spite of an improbable coincidence of circumstances (such is his fate, such is the will of God).

title_en: Missed the money with his eyes closed
description_en: Gold is left in a man's way so that he would make use of it. At that moment the man happens to close his eyes and walks past.

title_en: Birds set the town on fire

description_en: A guard (courtier) agrees to let a man in to a powerful person on condition that the man gives him half of the expected reward. The man asks for a beating as his reward or expected one from the start.

title_en: The little mouse in the bowl
description_en: Poor people blame Adam and Eve for their misfortunes. A powerful person gives them an opportunity to live in comfort on condition that they do not break a certain taboo (usually not to open a certain vessel). They are unable to resist the temptation, after which they are returned to their former state.

title_en: Every deception is the beginning of the next
description_en: A person harms others one after another in such a way that each deceived one is used as a tool to harm the next.
In episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or antisocial behaviour the raven (crow) is the main trickster (no less than three different episodes).
Because of its stupidity or antisocial behaviour the fox (jackal) perishes or suffers damage.
In episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is a jay.
The crayfish (crab) defeats or deceives strong adversaries by cunning.

title_en: The turtle (toad, frog) is the winning trickster
description_en: A turtle (a toad, a frog) defeats strong adversaries thanks to its smartness or persistence. The character is named if it is a toad or a frog; in the other cases it is a turtle.
Because of its stupidity or antisocial behaviour the monkey perishes or suffers damage.

title_en: The dwarf deer is the winning trickster
description_en: A character defeats or outwits strong adversaries thanks to its smartness. The protagonists are dwarf ungulates, usually the duiker or the mouse-deer, which are taxonomically far from each other but look alike. In some publications on African traditions it is difficult to tell which animal is meant, but these are certainly small even-toed ungulates, usually (always?) duikers.

title_en: The jaguar (ocelot, puma) is a failure
description_en: Because of its stupidity or antisocial behavior the jaguar (puma, ocelot) perishes or suffers damage. The character is named if it is a puma or an ocelot; in the other cases it is a jaguar.
The hero of the narrative is a person nicknamed "the Beardless" (Köse, Kösa, Kose, Kusa, Kusu).
The hero of the narrative is a bald man (hence his usual nickname: Taz, Taschi, Kal, Keloğlan, Kechal, etc.).

title_en: The Gypsy is the winning trickster
description_en: A Gypsy defeats or deceives strong adversaries by cunning.

title_en: The Gypsy is the adversary and loser
description_en: A Gypsy man (and more often a Gypsy woman) is the antagonist or (rarely) a weak loser. The hero (heroine) gets the better of him (her).
A hen (or another bird) lays eggs, boils them and feeds other persons (who try to imitate her with sad consequences for themselves).
A smith is (allegedly) able to make people young again and to make maimed people and animals whole.

title_en: Reforging the old into the young: a failed imitation
description_en: A person (supposedly) reforges (boils, dismembers) a human being, returning youth (health, life) to him. Another tries to imitate him without success.

title_en: Cuts off the horse's leg to shoe it
description_en: To shoe a horse or a donkey, Jesus (a saint) cuts off its leg, nails a horseshoe to the hoof and puts the leg back. Another person tries to imitate him without success.

title_en: The old woman turned into a monkey
description_en: A smith presumptuously tries to reforge an old woman into a young one (an old man into a youth). A magic helper brings the killed woman back to life but only in the shape of an animal, as a rule a monkey.
A person who is something fatty (a sausage, a piece of fat, etc.) cooks tasty food flavouring it with its own fat. Another decides to act in the same way and perishes.

title_en: The fool puts a needle into the hay
description_en: The fool puts a small sharp object (a needle, a pin, a nail) in a place where it cannot be found afterwards (hay, a sack of flour, etc.).

title_en: The fool buys spoons and a table
description_en: A fool buys spoons and/or a table, tells the table to walk on its own legs and throws away the spoons because they rattle. The two episodes are usually combined.
Having bought salt or sugar, a fool pours it into a body of water to salt or sweeten the water.
Fools plant meat, horns or bones hoping to grow animals.
Having forgotten his name, a fool recalls it when he happens to hear a certain word.

title_en: The fool takes care of tree stumps
description_en: A fool decides that tree stumps need caps and puts pots on the stumps.

title_en: The fool sells property to frogs
description_en: A fool (a woman or a man) throws valuables into the water believing that the croaking frogs will make use of them.

title_en: The foolish woman throws away the yarn
description_en: A foolish woman throws away her yarn (into the water, into the bushes) believing that somebody will turn it into cloth.

title_en: The fool's talk with a bird
description_en: Hearing the cry of a bird (often an owl), a fool believes that the bird is talking to him and as a result finds a treasure.

title_en: The fool sells goods to a lizard
description_en: A fool sells his goods to a lizard believing that the buyer will pay. Trying to get the money, he finds a treasure.

title_en: The fool sells goods to a tree
description_en: A fool sells his goods to a tree (stump, post, a cross in the field) believing that the buyer will pay. Trying to get the money, he finds a treasure.

title_en: The fool sells goods to a statue
description_en: A fool sells his goods to a statue believing that the buyer will pay. Trying to get the money, he finds a treasure.

title_en: The fool sells goods to dogs
description_en: A fool sells his goods to dogs believing that the buyers will pay. Trying to get the money, he finds a treasure.
A trickster (using a naive simpleton or a foolish woman) manages to get hold of the treasures loaded on a stray camel.
A fool notices the fontanelle on a baby's head, takes it for a boil and squeezes it. The baby falls silent and the fool thinks that it has fallen asleep.

title_en: The judge who lost an eye
description_en: A husband has found a treasure. He knows that his wife will blab about it. To make people disbelieve her, the husband says, and the wife later repeats, that the judge was hurt (lost an eye, has sores on his face) by the hail (the soup that poured from the sky) that fell at that time. The furious judge drives the woman away and the treasure remains with the husband.

Understanding that his wife will bring trouble on the family by telling the truth, a husband says that the sounds she hears are the screams of the landlord (an official, etc.) who is being beaten, dragged to hell, etc. She repeats this to the landlord (official) and he declares her insane.

title_en: Is the harvest eaten? Is the dead man dead?
description_en: A man asks another whether the grain they see has already been eaten and/or whether the dead man who is being carried to the grave is alive. It turns out that his questions make sense.
A girl gently (allegorically) reproaches a visitor for having entered the house suddenly or regrets that there is no dog to warn of a guest's coming.

title_en: Misunderstood instructions: washing with boiling water
description_en: Told to wash an old person with warm water, a fool scalds him with boiling water.
A fool or a jester takes the house door off its hinges and drags it along.

title_en: Drops a heavy object from the tree
description_en: A man (often a fool or a jester) drops a (heavy) object from a tree. The (dangerous) persons under the tree run away in fright leaving their valuables.
The one hiding in a tree cuts off (bites off) a dangerous person's tongue by a cunning trick, and that person cannot tell his companions anything.
One person asks another to put parsley and/or onion into the soup. The other understands (pretends to understand) the words as if he were to kill a child (dog) named Parsley (Onion).
A fool does not pull his trousers or boots on but jumps into them from above.
Instead of gathering nuts into a basket or shovelling them with a spade, a fool rakes them with a pitchfork.
Trying to seize the hare, another animal tears off (bites off) its tail. Since then it is short.

An old man carries a trough and lies down to rest covering himself with it. Beasts take the trough for a table and bring food. The old man gets up, the beasts run away and the food goes to the old man.
A person advises another to plant or sow boiled or roasted seeds or tubers, and the other follows the advice.

To obtain or return valuables, a person turns into a baby or into a small object from contact with which a woman becomes pregnant. The baby picked up by the woman or born to her takes his true shape and steals the valuables (or makes the girl who picked him up pregnant, if that was his aim).
A child is promised (and given) the sun (and/or the moon) as a toy.
When a beauty walks on the ground, jewels appear, flowers bloom, etc. under her feet.
Instead of the usual excretions, beads, flowers, gold and other valuables pour from a man's body; or valuables appear thanks to the very presence of a male person.
Instead of the usual excretions, beads, flowers, gold and other valuables pour from a woman's body; or valuables appear thanks to the very presence of a female person.
A man fights a bear or (Malayali) a leopard and makes another man believe that this animal defecates gold.
A land animal (usually a rat) is drowning (remains on an islet), reaches the shore with the help of another animal and repays it with ingratitude.
The octopus or the starfish was covered with hair but the rat gnawed it off.

title_en: The squirrel and the little fish
description_en: Showing agility and inventiveness, a squirrel and a little fish obtain medicines for each other.

title_en: The sham doctor: the scoundrel punished
description_en: Taking revenge for the property taken from him (a domestic animal or bird), the hero comes to the offender many times in different guises (a girl, a doctor, etc.) and cruelly torments him.
The crow promises to cure the fish but eats it.
A person provokes a quarrel by telling each of his adversaries how one of them allegedly spoke of the other in a hostile or insulting way.
Having eaten a certain food, the trickster leaves a mountain of excrement that is bigger than he is.

title_en: A fire at the night camp in the forest
description_en: A young man or a girl spends a night in the forest. One of the forest dwellers has fire. After the hero or the heroine does something wrong, this fire disappears.

title_en: The long return: agouti at the house
description_en: A man has lost his way and on the way home meets various creatures. When he comes to the agouti (Dasyprocta), it becomes clear that his home is already near.
Two persons compare their excrement (for different purposes). One of them manages to switch it.
Having noticed the beautiful plumage of the woodpecker, the wolf or the bear believes that the fox painted it and asks the fox to make him just as handsome. The fox burns him alive.

God (a saint) travels with a companion. When he is away, the companion eats the kidneys (heart, etc.) and says that the animal had no kidneys. He persists (even in the face of death) but confesses when he is promised riches.

title_en: Divides by biting off a piece at a time
description_en: Two persons ask a third to divide something edible between them. He bites off a little from each of the halves because now one and now the other is slightly bigger. As a result he eats everything.
A person attracts and catches carrion eaters (usually birds) and as a result obtains valuables or returns something valuable (fire, a woman, animals, etc.).

title_en: The Trojan Horse: victory over enemies
description_en: Enemies are shown a figure of a horse or a bull, life-size or larger. Not understanding that it is a trick, they bring the figure to their territory and as a result are defeated.

title_en: The Trojan horse: winning a woman
description_en: To win a woman, the hero hides inside a hollow figure of a hoofed animal or in an animal's carcass. The person who guards the woman himself delivers this object to her. The hero gets out and becomes the woman's lover. Or a woman hides inside the figure of an animal that is delivered to a man's chambers.
Having wished for a child, a childless woman gives birth to a multitude of tiny boys. She herself or her husband kills them or throws them away, but one remains and helps his parents.

title_en: The boy is a chopped-off finger
description_en: A tiny man emerges from a chopped-off finger.
A tiny boy (rarely a girl) emerges from a pea (bean, grain) or from a pellet of goat dung; he is almost as small as a pea. Or he was born after his mother ate a pea.
A tiny boy emerges from an animal's ear, he is compared in size to an ear, his name is "Ear".

When a woman falls asleep, a prankster (usually a tiny boy) puts beside her an embryo or an animal's entrails or something similar so that the woman herself or others would think that she has had a miscarriage or that her entrails have fallen out.
When the inhabitants of a house fall asleep, a prankster (usually a tiny boy) ties them together in pairs so that they would quarrel when they wake up.

title_en: The luminaries float above the hero
description_en: A person gets to a place from which he cannot get out. As celestial luminaries (no less than three different ones) float past him or above him, he notices them (and asks them for help).

A zoomorphic person waits to be carried across a body of water or brought down from a height. Animals or fish offer help one after another. The person chooses the last one: he was waiting for it in order to eat it.

title_en: The journey to the fish's country
description_en: A man visits the country from which the salmon come to people.

A person carefully preserves the bones of eaten migratory birds (and not of fish or animals) and the birds come to life again. (Episodes of reviving a domestic goose or cock in realistic tales of type ATU 571 are not counted; see motif M84b3).
A husband brings his wife a bird that slaughters and cooks itself and then is reborn from the gnawed bones. When the wife's lover comes to her, they both stick to the bird.
A tree is described on which jewels or ornaments hang instead of fruits; different parts of the tree are made of different metals or (semi)precious stones.
Golden fruits (more rarely only leaves) of a certain tree, usually golden apples, are mentioned in the narrative.
Possession of certain fruits (usually apples) ensures eternal youth.
A man sells a cap to others having convinced them that it pays the bill: one only has to raise it (throw it on the floor, etc.). In fact he paid the innkeeper in advance.
When enemies come to deal with a man, he pretends to be dead.
One person suggests that another slide down a hill in order to destroy him. Cf. motif L42C.

title_en: Sliding down a hill: the antagonist's victims
description_en: A demonic person destroys his victims by provoking them to slide down a hill.

title_en: Sliding down a hill: animal tricksters
description_en: Through stupidity or carelessness a zoomorphic person slides down a hill and as a result perishes or suffers damage (is impaled on a point, falls into the water, etc.).

title_en: The wolf under the mill wheel
description_en: A person is lured into looking under a mill wheel and perishes or is maimed.

title_en: The blinded one questions the trees to get new eyes
description_en: Having lost his sight, a person walks bumping into trees of different species until he finds the one with the help of which he makes himself (gets) new eyes.

title_en: The blinded one questions the trees to reach water
description_en: Having lost his sight, a person walks asking trees of different species who they are and thus learns how far the water is.
The roots (belt) of mountains or stones are mentioned in myths, riddles, spells and songs as something that does not exist in reality.
The coming of late autumn and then of winter follows the departure of two or three species of birds that fly in a wedge (Zugvögel).
It is said about a bird-like person that he sits on several trees.

title_en: Drives the adversary into the ground
description_en: A hero drives his adversary into the ground, or he and his adversary drive each other into the ground in turn (up to the ankles, up to the waist, etc.).
Streams (jets) that consist not of water but of honey (honey and butter, butter and milk, milk and blood) are mentioned as a sign of generosity and abundance. Cf. motifs H16 – H16B, K33F.
Somewhere rivers of milk flow between banks of kissel (porridge): a sign of abundance (impossible in reality). Cf. motif H16B.

title_en: Higher than the forest, lower than the clouds

description_en: A person asks those around which object (usually a key) is better, the old one (lost and found) or the new one. A forgotten and regained marriage partner is meant (more rarely the question is asked directly).
The image of a rope twisted threefold describes the invincibility of two united friends.

title_en: The liver sank and the lungs floated away
description_en: A tale or an epic text ends with a formula saying that the liver sank and the lungs floated away (floated up, remained, etc.).
